name: Mt Himlung Expedition
climbingGrade: Alpine PD — glacier travel with fixed lines above Base Camp
summitSuccessNotes: Best summit window is mid-September to mid-October; two rotations through High Camp materially improve success odds.
summary: A remote 7,000m peak above the restricted Nar-Phu valley, climbed via glacier travel and fixed lines — technical enough to test experienced climbers, without the crowds of the 8,000m circuit.
highlights: Summit views across the Manang Himal

itinerary.title: Drive to Koto
itinerary.description: A long, scenic drive from Kathmandu up the Marsyangdi valley to Koto, the gateway to the restricted Nar-Phu valley.

itinerary.title: Koto to Meta
itinerary.description: Enter the restricted Nar-Phu valley, following the Nar Khola gorge through pine forest and cliffside trail.

itinerary.title: Meta to Phu Gaon
itinerary.description: Climb through narrowing gorge walls into the fortress-like village of Phu Gaon, one of the most remote settlements in Nepal.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization day in Phu Gaon
itinerary.description: A rest day to explore Phu's gompa and let the body adjust before pushing higher toward Base Camp.

itinerary.title: Phu Gaon to Himlung Base Camp
itinerary.description: Leave the last permanent settlement behind and follow moraine trail to Base Camp beneath Himlung's south face.

itinerary.title: Base Camp acclimatization and rotation
itinerary.description: Rest, gear checks and a short rotation onto the lower glacier to prepare for the climb to High Camp.

itinerary.title: Base Camp to High Camp
itinerary.description: Rope up for the glacier crossing to High Camp, the last stop before the summit push.

itinerary.title: Summit day
itinerary.description: An early alpine start on fixed lines up the summit ridge, standing atop Himlung's 7,126m summit before descending to High Camp.

itinerary.title: Descend to Kathmandu
itinerary.description: Retrace the valley trail to Koto and drive back to Kathmandu for a celebratory dinner.

name: Ama Dablam Expedition
climbingGrade: Alpine AD — steep fixed-rope sections above Camp 2
summitSuccessNotes: One of the most photogenic 6,000ers in the world; the Yellow Tower and Mushroom Ridge sections demand solid jumaring technique.
summary: The iconic sculpted peak above Tengboche — a technical, fixed-rope climb with some of the most exposed camps in the Himalaya.
highlights: Classic Khumbu approach via Namche and Tengboche
The Yellow Tower and Mushroom Ridge pitches
Summit views of Everest, Lhotse and Makalu

itinerary.title: Fly to Lukla, trek to Phakding
itinerary.description: A dramatic mountain flight into Lukla, then an easy walk down the Dudh Koshi valley to Phakding.

itinerary.title: Phakding to Namche Bazaar
itinerary.description: Cross the Hillary suspension bridges and climb steeply into the Sherpa capital, Namche Bazaar.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization day in Namche
itinerary.description: A rest day with a short hike up to the Everest View Hotel for first sight of the big peaks.

itinerary.title: Namche to Tengboche
itinerary.description: A rolling trail with the first full view of Ama Dablam's sculpted ridgeline, ending at Tengboche's famous monastery.

itinerary.title: Tengboche to Pangboche
itinerary.description: Descend through rhododendron forest and climb again to Pangboche, home to the Khumbu's oldest monastery.

itinerary.title: Pangboche to Ama Dablam Base Camp
itinerary.description: Leave the main trekking trail and climb moraine to Base Camp, pitched directly beneath the peak's south-west ridge.

itinerary.title: Base Camp acclimatization and rotation
itinerary.description: Rest, technical gear checks, and a rotation partway up the ridge to fix ropes and pre-acclimatize.

itinerary.title: Base Camp to Camp 2
itinerary.description: Climb the exposed granite ridge past Camp 1 to Camp 2's dramatically perched tent platforms.

itinerary.title: Summit day
itinerary.description: Jumar the fixed ropes through the Yellow Tower and Mushroom Ridge to the summit, with Everest and Lhotse filling the skyline.

itinerary.title: Descend to Lukla, fly to Kathmandu
itinerary.description: A long descent day back down the valley to Lukla, followed by the flight home to Kathmandu.

name: Island Peak Expedition
climbingGrade: Trekking peak — glacier walk with a fixed-rope headwall near the summit
summitSuccessNotes: The most accessible 6,000m summit in the Khumbu — strong trek fitness plus a day of basic ice-climbing training is normally enough.
summary: Nepal's most popular trekking peak — a glacier walk to a fixed-rope headwall, with sweeping views of Lhotse, Makalu and Ama Dablam from the summit ridge.
highlights: Glacier crossing on the Lhotse Nup Glacier
Fixed-rope headwall to the summit ridge
Views of four 8,000m peaks from the top

itinerary.title: Fly to Lukla, trek to Phakding
itinerary.description: A dramatic mountain flight into Lukla, then an easy walk down the Dudh Koshi valley to Phakding.

itinerary.title: Phakding to Namche Bazaar
itinerary.description: Cross the Hillary suspension bridges and climb steeply into the Sherpa capital, Namche Bazaar.

itinerary.title: Namche to Tengboche
itinerary.description: A rolling trail with wide Himalayan views, ending at Tengboche's famous monastery.

itinerary.title: Tengboche to Dingboche
itinerary.description: Follow the Imja Khola valley up into drier, higher terrain, with Ama Dablam close overhead.

itinerary.title: Dingboche to Chhukung
itinerary.description: A short, high acclimatization walk to Chhukung, the last village before Island Peak's approach.

itinerary.title: Chhukung to Island Peak Base Camp
itinerary.description: Cross moraine below the Lhotse Nup Glacier to Base Camp, with a climbing-technique refresher on arrival.

itinerary.title: Summit day
itinerary.description: An early start across the glacier and up the fixed-rope headwall to the summit ridge, with Lhotse, Makalu and Ama Dablam all visible from the top.

itinerary.title: Descend to Lukla, fly to Kathmandu
itinerary.description: A long descent back down the valley to Lukla, followed by the flight home to Kathmandu.
